title: Analytical and Experimental Study of the Degradation Factor by Accelerated Aging in AISI 4140 Steels in the Food Industry
content: The study of fracture mechanics has had a very high development, from its formal origins in 1820 with the studies on failures in railway axles or in 1860 where the first investigations were carried out on failure under fatigue cycles, but it was not until 1961 in Paris, when it was recognized that all structures can fail due to these causes and that the cracks that are generated during the periods of useful life propagate with stress values much lower than the critical values. The different mathematical models used by Inglish, A. A. Griffith, L. A. Wigglesworth, Irwin adequately describe the behavior of fractures and in more contemporary studies Dr. G. M. Urriolagoitia Calderon and Dr. G. Urriolagoitia Sosa, generated models to predict the direction and propagation of the fracture by analyzing the behavior of the maximum and minimum principal stress and its relationship with shear stresses [1]. This study considers two important initial aspects, the first consideration is that for the generation of accelerated aging the conditions set by the ASTM B-117 standard were established, with respect to the temperature control that was given at 40°C this acts within the salt spray chamber at 5% +/- 1 by weight and the application of UV radiation with a wavelength of 200 nm to 400 nm applying the sequences indicated by the standard. [2] The second consideration taken was that as a result of the attack on the material, which generated an intensifier point of efforts where the microscopy study shown in Figure 1 was performed.
